title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 651–653 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche' notes). G is a group scheme over S. A section g is 'generically unipotent'. The question is whether g comes from a homomorphism G_a → G. Over the generic point η (characteristic 0) a unipotent g_η equals φ_η(1) for a unique φ_η: G_{a,η} → G_η. So the question is whether φ_η extends over S.

Grothendieck reduces to a DVR A with fraction field K, and to G ⊂ GL(M) with M free of rank n. Write g_η = exp(X), with X ∈ End(M)⊗K and X^n = 0. The hypothesis is (9): exp(X) and exp(−X) are integral. The extension question is (10): is X^i/i! integral for all i < n? In that case φ(λ) = Σ λ^i X^i/i! is a polynomial over A.

On the previous page he dismisses n = 2 and n = 3 as trivial. For n = 4, condition (11) is X^2/2 ± X^3/6 ∈ M_4(A), and the question (12) is whether X^2/2 and X^3/6 are integral. This is clear when 2 is invertible.

On this page he isolates residue characteristic 2, with 2 a uniformizer (e.g. A = Z_2). He writes X = 2^{−ν}X_0 with X_0 primitive integral. This turns (11) into (11 bis) and the question into (12 bis); in (12 bis) the factor 1/6 is replaced by 1/2, which is harmless since 3 is a unit. He notes the answer is trivially yes if X_0^3 = 0, so the interesting case is when g_η is 'tout principal' unipotent, i.e. a single Jordan block of size 4.

He then admits he needs either a counterexample or a theorem. He retreats to a weaker statement, headed in the margin 'Essai de construction des sections génériquement unipotentes'. For G locally of finite presentation over a generically reduced S, a section g is generically unipotent iff there exist n > 0 and a homomorphism φ: G_a → G with φ(1) = g^n. (The next page's transcription writes G_m, but in context this must be G_a.) The proof begun on the next page splits into two cases. If the generic characteristic is p > 0, g_η has finite order and φ is trivial. In characteristic 0 he takes the generic exponential φ_{1η} and its domain of definition U, then passes to g^n, i.e. φ_{nη}(λ) = φ_{1η}(nλ), to enlarge the domain.

Modern verdict: the answer to (12) is NO, and the obstruction already occurs for n = 3. Take u = 1 + J ∈ GL_r(Z_p), with J a single nilpotent Jordan block, so X = log u. Then exp(λX) = Σ_i C(λ,i) J^i. This is an integer-valued polynomial in λ but not a polynomial over Z_(p) once r − 1 ≥ p. So φ_η does not extend, although u and u^{-1} are integral.

Passing to g^n multiplies X by n. Then n^i X^i/i! becomes integral for a suitable n, e.g. n divisible by (r−1)!. This is exactly why the 'g^n' version of the theorem holds over a DVR in mixed characteristic.
errors: Grothendieck's claim on the previous page that n = 3 is 'trivial' is false unless X is assumed integral. Over Z_2, take u = 1 + J_3 and X = log u = J − J^2/2. Then exp(±X) = 1 ± J (the J^2 terms cancel), which is integral, but X and X^2/2 = J^2/2 are not. This already gives a counterexample to the analogue of (10).

For n = 4 the answer to (12)/(12 bis) is negative. Take u = 1 + J_4 over Z_2 and X = log u = J − J^2/2 + J^3/3. Then u and u^{-1} are integral, but X^2/2 = J^2/2 − J^3/2 is not. More conceptually, exp(λ log u) = Σ C(λ,i) J^i is integer-valued but not polynomial over Z_2. The counterexample Grothendieck says he lacks is thus elementary.
In (12 bis) the coefficient of X_0^3 is written 1/2 instead of 1/6. This is harmless, since 3 is a unit in A.

The stated 'theorem' over an arbitrary generically reduced S, locally of finite presentation, is only sketched. Over a DVR the g^n version is fine. The general case (non-affine or non-flat G, non-integral S, extending φ beyond the opens U_n) is left to 'dévissages faciles' that are not done, so the proof is incomplete.

ideas.what: Criterion for a generically unipotent section to extend to a homomorphism G_a → G: integrality of all divided powers X^i/i! of the logarithm.
ideas.modern_name: Integral exponential / extension of the Springer–exponential map over Z_(p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (divided powers). Integral exponentials in good characteristic: Serre (1990s), Seitz, McNinch, Sobaje.
ideas.where_published: SGA3 discusses unipotent elements and G_a-actions but, as far as I know, not this exact question.

ideas.what: Obstruction to the extension: exp(λ log u) = Σ C(λ,i) N^i is integer-valued rather than polynomial in λ.
ideas.modern_name: Integer-valued polynomials / binomial rings; the affine group scheme Spec Int(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pólya and Ostrowski (integer-valued polynomials); Elliott (binomial rings); Toën (schematization via Spec Int(Z), 2020).

ideas.what: Theorem: g is generically unipotent iff some power g^n equals φ(1) for a homomorphism φ: G_a → G.
ideas.modern_name: Unipotent elements up to a power lie in one-parameter additive subgroups (integral form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; related to work on unipotent elements of group schemes over Z (e.g. the Proud/Sobaje line).

missed.claim: The failure Grothendieck is probing is precisely that a unipotent section over Z_(p) naturally comes from the binomial group scheme H = Spec Int(Z) (integer-valued polynomials), not from G_a. Passing to g^n corresponds to the map G_a → H. This group scheme is the one Toën later used for Grothendieck's own 'schématisation' problem. The page thus implicitly meets the object that later answered a question from Pursuing Stacks, though Grothendieck does not identify it here.
missed.quote: Pour en avoir le cœur net, il faudrait un contrexemple ... ou un théorème!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically suggestive: it shows Grothendieck running into the integer-valued/binomial phenomenon inside group-scheme questions. This is a modest observation rather than a new result.

missed.claim: The general theorem over a generically reduced base, locally of finite presentation, is left with unexecuted 'dévissages'.
missed.quote: Théorème (!) Soit G un schéma en groupes loc. de présentation finie sur un schéma S génériquement réduit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low impact: the statement is standard-looking and its DVR case is easy.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine exploratory computation on integrality of exponentials. The open question Grothendieck poses has an elementary negative answer (1 + Jordan block), and his fallback 'g^n' theorem is folklore-level. The only mild interest is the implicit link to binomial / integer-valued-polynomial group schemes.
transcription_corrections: 'g_y' (here and on the previous page) should almost certainly be g_η, the generic fibre of g.
'unip. tout principal' means 'unipotent principal', i.e. a single Jordan block (regular unipotent).
The marginal '(s. f. p. sur S)' likely reads '(séparé de prés. finie sur S)' or '(loc. de prés. finie)'; reading uncertain.
On the next page 'φ: G_m → G' should read G_a, as the context (unipotent, φ_{1η}(nλ)) requires.
In (12 bis) the image reads 1/2 in both terms; the mathematically consistent version is 1/2·X_0^2/2^{2ν} and 1/6·X_0^3/2^{3ν}, which are equivalent since 3 is a unit.
